'''Svetlana Katok''' (born May 1, 1947)<ref>[https://dynkincollection.library.cornell.edu/biographies/863 Svetlana Katok], Eugene B. Dynkin Collection of Mathematics Interviews, Cornell University, January 1981, retrieved October 16, 2013.</ref> is a Russian-American mathematician and a professor of mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref name="awm">[http://www.awm-math.org/noetherbrochure/Katok04.html Svetlana Katok], Association for Women in Mathematics, 2005, retrieved October 16, 2013.</ref>

== Education and career ==
Katok grew up in [[Moscow]], and earned a master's degree from [[Moscow State University]] in 1969; however, due to the antisemitic and anti-intelligentsia policies of the time, she was denied admission to the doctoral program there and instead worked for several years in the area of early and secondary mathematical education.<ref name="awm" /> She immigrated to the US in 1978,<ref name="awm" /> and earned her doctorate from the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in 1983 under the supervision of [[Don Zagier]].<ref name="awm" /><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=36934}}</ref> She joined the [[Pennsylvania State University]] faculty in 1990.<ref name="awm" />

Katok founded the Electronic Research Announcements of the American Mathematical Society in 1995; it was renamed in 2007 to the Electronic Research Announcements in Mathematical Sciences, and she remains its managing editor.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/publications/journals/journalsframework/era Electronic Research Announcements], retrieved October 16, 2013.</ref>

Katok was an [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Council member at large.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=March 27, 2023 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Books ==
Katok is the author of:
*''Fuchsian Groups'', Chicago Lectures in Mathematics, [[University of Chicago Press]], 1992.<ref>Review of ''Fuchsian Groups'' by [[Irwin Kra]], 1993, {{MR|1177168}}.</ref> Russian edition, [[Faktorial Press]], Moscow, 2002.
*''p-adic Analysis Compared with Real'', Student Mathematical Library, vol. 37, American Math. Soc., 2007.<ref>Review of ''p-adic Analysis'' by Daniel Barsky, 2008, {{MR|2298943}}.</ref> Russian edition, MCCME Press, Moscow, 2004.
Additionally, she coedited the book ''MASS Selecta: Teaching and learning advanced undergraduate mathematics'' (American Math. Soc., 2003).<ref>Unsigned review of ''MASS Selecta'', 2004, {{MR|2027171}}.</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Katok was the 2004 [[Noether Lecture|Emmy Noether Lecturer]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref name="awm" /> In 2012 she and her husband, mathematician [[Anatole Katok]], both became [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]. Retrieved October 16, 2013. [[American Mathematical Society]].</ref>
